description: Plays one MPX part on a physically modelled cello: four bowed strings on a bridge and body. A bow-friction model drives the strings, and a performance model sets each note's bow force, speed and position.

params.name: Vibrato
params.text: Vibrato width, relative to each note's default. At the centre, the default: wider on long and loud notes, none on open strings or notes marked senza vibrato, and narrower in music from earlier periods. Fully counter-clockwise, no vibrato; fully clockwise, twice the default. Changes apply immediately, including to notes already sounding.

params.name: Brightness
params.text: Cuts frequencies above about 1.2 kHz, by up to 12 dB when fully counter-clockwise. Fully clockwise, no cut. A filter on the output only; it does not change how notes are played.

inputs.name: MPX note
inputs.text: The part to play, from mpxScore or any other MPX source. While connected, the Gate, 1V/oct, Level and Vibrato CV inputs are ignored.

inputs.name: Gate
inputs.text: Plays a note while the gate is above 1 V and releases it when the gate falls below 0.5 V. With a polyphonic gate, the highest pitch among the channels whose gate is high is played. Notes from this input are played without advance simulation, as at Fidelity level 4. Ignored while an MPX cable is connected.

inputs.name: 1V/oct
inputs.text: Pitch of the note played from the Gate input, 1 V per octave, 0 V = C4. A change of more than half a semitone while the gate stays high starts a new note, slurred in the same bow stroke. Smaller changes are ignored; the note keeps its pitch.

inputs.name: Level
inputs.text: Dynamic of each note played from the Gate input, read when the note starts. 0 V is ppp and 10 V is fff; pp, p, mp, mf, f and ff fall at equal steps of about 1.43 V between them, and voltages in between give intermediate levels. Unconnected: mf.

inputs.name: Vibrato CV
inputs.text: Added to the Vibrato knob's setting: +5 V adds the same amount as the knob's centre position. The total is limited to between no vibrato and twice the default width. Ignored while an MPX cable is connected.

outputs.name: Out
outputs.text: Mono audio. Its loudness matches mpxPiano playing the same dynamics; a single fff note peaks at about 2.7 V.

lights.name: Level
lights.text: Flashes green when a note starts. Orange when the output exceeds 7.07 V, 3 dB below clipping; red when it reaches 10 V, where Rack's audio interface clips.

notes: mpxScore sends each note to the module 4.5 seconds before it sounds. At Fidelity levels 1 to 3, the module uses that time to simulate the note's attack. Notes from sources that do not send them in advance, such as a keyboard or a sequencer, are played as they arrive.

Each module models one player. Two notes on adjacent strings are bowed together as a double stop. Three- or four-note chords are broken: the lower two notes sound briefly, then the bow moves to the upper two. Plucked chords are strummed upwards. Chord notes that cannot be fingered together are dropped, lowest first. With a polyphonic gate, only the highest channel whose gate is high is played. For a section, use one module per player.

Notes in a passage marked pizz. are plucked, up to the next arco. The string is plucked between the end of the fingerboard and the bridge, with a strength set by the dynamic. A plucked string rings until it decays or is played again, regardless of the written note length. Notes marked + (left-hand pizzicato) are plucked 16 dB quieter and damped at their written end. A string still ringing has its vibration reduced to a quarter before it is plucked again. Plucked notes are not simulated in advance. Notes from the Gate input are always bowed.

If a part goes below the lowest open string, the whole part is played one or two octaves higher, as far as its highest note allows. If it goes above the end of the fingerboard, two octaves and a sixth above the highest open string, the whole part is played one or two octaves lower. Notes still out of range, and notes from the Gate input, are moved individually by octaves. While a part is out of range, the light on the cable plug at the source's MPX output blinks.

Fidelity, in the right-click menu, sets how much of each note's attack is simulated in advance, on a second copy of the instrument model. Level 1 simulates up to 18 attack variants for each note and 3 for each bow change: the most computing. Level 2 simulates 2 attack variants for each note. Level 3 simulates only bow changes, 3 variants each. Level 4, the default, simulates nothing, so notes need not be sent in advance: the least computing.

Enable diagnostics, in the right-click menu, shows a counter at the top of the panel. On by default. The counter shows how many notes sent in advance were played without their simulation, because it had not finished in time; a busy computer is the usual cause. Notes not sent in advance are not counted. It resets to 0 when Fidelity, Economy or the part's range changes, or when the source returns to its start, and stays at 0 at level 4.

Economy, in the right-click menu, roughly halves the computing at some cost in sound quality: the strings are computed at half the internal sample rate, and a string that is not being played stops being computed once it falls silent, so it no longer resonates with the other strings.
